introduction.about: I'm a software engineer with 3 years of experience in development and testing. I take pride in building things that work well and look good. I have a broad range of experience across project planning, development, manual and automated testing and release management.
introduction.about2: I pride myself on not creating rubbish software, so I understand a project from the first line of code through to delivery. I enjoy solving technical problems and learning new technologies, however I get the most satisfaction working with teams of great people and making lifelong connections with those I work with.

experience1.title: Software Engineer
experience1.skills: Full-Stack Development, C#, VB.NET, SQL, Migration Development, AI development
experience1.content: I work as a full-stack developer on both legacy and greenfield projects. I'm comfortable moving between older code and fresh exciting new stuff. Lately I've been using AI-driven development orchestrating numerous agents to make some incredible new things!

experience2.title: Software Engineering Analyst
experience2.skills: Web Development, SQL, Javascript, Java, Selenium, Integration Testing
experience2.content: I built and tested software as part of large project teams, which taught me how much careful testing matters. I worked with some incredible people and helped set up the Accenture Ballarat office from scratch, an amazing experience I'm all the better for having been a part of. The role gave me solid experience working with Java, SQL, JavaScript, and Selenium in industry settings.

experience3.title: Software Developer Intern
experience3.skills: Front-End Web Development, TypeScript, React, Next.js, C#, SQL, Sitecore CMS
experience3.content: My internship with Diversus was an incredible opportunity where I was paid to learn amongst some wonderful people and experience a welcoming and inclusive environment that I don't think can ever be beaten! This was where I started building front end websites with React, Next.js, and Sitecore CMS. It's where I first got hooked on making interfaces that look good and work well and where I first broke a production release (well only for an hour or two!).
